records.statement: up creates a container from the resolved configuration such that a subsequent exec observes the expected environment and remote user, matching the reference.
records.notes: Backed by case-up-exec-parity (parity_up_exec, a single reported outcome shared with bhv-exec-container-id-metadata) and, independently, by the declarative case-up-exec-decl-traditional (023 T040).

records.statement: A Feature that cannot be installed — its install script exiting non-zero, or a dependency graph with no resolvable order — fails `up` rather than producing a container without the Feature.
records.notes: Authored by the 024 US4 error-path tier. Deliberately separate from `bhv-up-feature-install-order`: that claim is about WHICH Features run and in what order on the success path, and an implementation that gets the order right while swallowing a failing install script satisfies it and not this one — the container it hands back looks complete and is missing the Feature. Both halves of the statement are exercised (a failing `install.sh`, and a two-Feature `dependsOn` cycle) because the two fail at different points: one inside the install, one before any install runs. Verified against oracle 0.87.0 — both sides fail on both inputs.

records.statement: `up` installs the configuration's Features into the container it creates, in the resolved install order, across image, Dockerfile, and Compose configuration sources.
records.notes: Evidenced by a live differential on the outcome plus a spec-expectation case that reads the marker each Feature's install.sh writes INSIDE the container — the lesson from the --image-name defect, where an outcome-only assertion reported success for an image with no Feature in it.

records.statement: Re-entering a workspace whose container already exists reattaches to it rather than creating a second one, including when the configuration has changed since it was created.
records.notes: Asserted as a metamorphic relationship (`first-create-vs-restart`) rather than against a fixed output, because what is being pinned is the relation between the two runs and not either run's document. The container-graph observation captures EVERY container matching the workspace label so a duplicate is visible; an exit code cannot show one.
